title: A natural mutation of timeless enhances mosquito thermal adaptation and malaria parasite transmission
title_zh: timeless 基因的天然突变增强蚊子热适应性与疟原虫传播
abstract: Anopheles stephensi, a malaria-transmitting mosquito, has invaded Africa and rapidly adapts to the high temperatures in urban settings. However, the molecular basis of its thermal adaptation remains unclear. Here, we identified a variant of a 5-kb deletion in the circadian clock gene timeless (tim-5kb) that rose to high frequency after 3 years of rearing at high laboratory temperatures. The tim+/-5kb heterozygous males maintain stable expression of the period gene at high temperatures, conferring a competitive mating advantage through the increased expression of the adipokinetic hormone gene AKH1 to promote energy mobilization and flight activity, together with the upregulation of fatty acyl-CoA reductase genes FAR3 and FAR5 to enhance the production of heptacosane pheromone. Moreover, heterozygous females exhibit increased susceptibility to Plasmodium infection, increasing malaria transmission potential. These findings reveal a circadian-based genetic mechanism that may underlie thermal adaptation in An. stephensi and hold important implications for malaria control in Africa.
abstract_zh: Anopheles stephensi 是一种疟疾传播蚊，已入侵非洲并迅速适应城市环境的高温，但其热适应的分子基础尚不清楚。本文在 circadian clock 基因 timeless（tim）中鉴别了一个 5-kb 缺失变异（tim-5kb），该变异在高温实验室饲养 3 年后频率显著升高。tim +/- 5kb 杂合雄性蚊在高温下能够维持 period 基因的稳定表达，通过上调脂肪动员激素基因 AKH1 促进能量动员和飞行活性，从而获得竞争性交配优势，同时上调脂肪酰基-CoA 还原酶基因 FAR3 和 FAR5，以增强庚三烷基信息素的产生。此外，杂合雌性蚊对疟原虫感染的易感性增加，从而提升疟疾传播潜力。这些发现揭示了一种可能支撑 An. stephensi 热适应的基于昼夜节律的遗传机制，对非洲疟疾控制具有重要意义。
